title: Tate twists
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-wf-weil-category]: distinct primes $p,\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $\Phi_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}((z\mapsto z^q)^{-1})$. Let $R=\mathcal O_E$ and choose a uniformizer $\varpi$. All sheaves below are on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the completed coefficient sheaf $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_X$ and the raw rational coefficient category $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(X,E)$ of [def-wf-weil-category]; in particular rational objects and arrows are obtained by inverting $\varpi$ on integral representatives. Write $P_E=\Phi_X^*$ for its completed, rationalized pullback, which in this automorphism case is exact coefficient transport as specified in that node.

For $r\geq1$ use the roots-of-unity sheaf [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]
$$
 \mu_{\ell^r,X}(U)=\{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:u^{\ell^r}=1\},
 \qquad t_r(u)=u^\ell.
$$
Using the sectionwise inverse limit of sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], define
$$
 \mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}(\mu_{\ell^r,X},t_r),
 \qquad L_R=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_X}(R)_X
$$
as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Parenthesized rings here denote discrete constant sheaves; the limit has its completed $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,X}$-action: if $b=(b_r)$ is a compatible coefficient section and $u=(u_r)$ a compatible root section, $(b\cdot u)_r=u_r^{b_r}$. Here exponentiation by $b_r$ means the action of $\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ on $\mu_{\ell^r,X}$. Give $L_R$ the resulting completed $B$-module structure of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], clauses 2 and 3. Define $E(1)$ to be the image of $L_R[0]$ in $\mathcal C_E$, and $E_X$ the image of $B[0]$. These integral objects belong to the integral coefficient category: $L_R$ is pro-etale locally free of rank one by that lemma, and $B$ is the free module of rank one, so the single-stratum perfect-complex criterion [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], with the complex $R[0]$, supplies precisely the bounded-constructible and compatible etale-origin conditions of [def-wf-weil-category]. The source notation
$$E(1)=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}E$$
means this integral scalar extension followed by rationalization, as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

Equip these objects with the following specified Weil maps. For every $r$, use the roots-of-unity pullback comparison $c_r:\Phi_X^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,X}\to\mu_{\ell^r,X}$ of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. It is an isomorphism, is semilinear over the canonical constant coefficient map, and commutes with $t_r$ by [lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso], clauses 1--3. Set
$$
 \tau_{\mathbf Z_\ell(1)}:
 \Phi_X^{-1}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_r\Phi_X^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,X}
 \xrightarrow{\varprojlim_r c_r}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_X,
$$
using preservation of limits by the site equivalence [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], clause 2. On $B$ take the map $\tau_B$ obtained from the same limit comparison and the canonical constant maps $\Phi_X^{-1}(R/\varpi^n)_X\cong(R/\varpi^n)_X$ of clause 3 of that node. On $L_R$ take the inverse-image tensor comparison [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] followed by $\tau_{\mathbf Z_\ell(1)}\otimes c_R$, with $c_R:\Phi_X^{-1}(R)_X\cong(R)_X$ the constant-ring map. This map is semilinear over $\tau_B$: after reduction its scalar identity is $c_r(b_r\cdot u_r)=c_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}(b_r)\cdot c_r(u_r)$ and the tensor balancing identity for $c_R$. Thus, after the completed coefficient identification in $P_E$, these are linear isomorphisms. Place them in degree zero and rationalize to obtain
$$\varphi_0:P_EE_X\xrightarrow{\sim}E_X,\qquad
\varphi_1:P_EE(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}E(1).$$
Hence $E_X$ and $E(1)$ denote the resulting Weil pairs when used in $\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)$.

Use the completed, rationalized derived tensor and its induced tensor Weil map of [def-wf-tensor-product], and the derived internal Hom and its conjugation Weil map of [def-wf-internal-hom]. Define
$$
 E(0)=E_X,\qquad E(m)=E(1)^{\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}m}\ (m>0),\qquad
 E(-m)=R\mathcal Hom_E(E(m),E_X)\ (m>0).
$$
The tensor power is the left-associated $m$-fold tensor, starting with $E(1)$ at $m=1$. The indicated tensor and internal-Hom arrows are exactly those of the cited definitions; in particular internal Hom uses the inverse of the first argument's Weil map contravariantly. Their restriction to Weil complexes is supplied by [lem-wf-tensor-weil] and [lem-wf-internal-hom-weil]. For every integer $m$, define the Tate twist functor by
$$
 (-)(m):\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E)\longrightarrow\mathrm{WeilD}(X_0,E),
 \qquad W\longmapsto W\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}E(m),\qquad
 u\longmapsto u\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{id}_{E(m)}.
$$
Functoriality and the commuting Weil square are the bifunctoriality in [lem-wf-tensor-weil].

lean.note: §1(B) dependency-interface repair. The former upstream TateTwist record defines a Qbar constant-twist model and provides neither the prescribed finite-field raw PBC category nor its scalar-extension functors. This module uses the existing PBC signed line sheaves and exact tensor, and the existing root-projection-normalized Frobenius signed maps, transports the maps through the canonical coefficient isomorphism, places them in degree zero and rationalizes in the unchanged PBC category. The resulting Weil pair and tensor functor retain the ordered positive powers, inverse-positive dual maps and all localized arrows. Only comparison maps uniquely determined by their section or integral-representative equations are selected; no arbitrary isomorphism or coefficient-category equivalence is chosen. The four postponed interface theorems concern the membership and canonical comparisons in this definition.

split_report.summary: Definition-only split with no new nodes. Unpacked the inherited finite-field/scheme/coefficient setting, roots-of-unity inverse limit and completed integral lattice, its raw rationalization, canonical Weil maps, all signed twists and the functor on arrows. Reused the integral stratified-perfect characterization to verify that rank-one lattices belong to the precise coefficient category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses. Reused existing tensor/internal-Hom constructions and restriction statements, never the circular twist-compatibility node. The old recorded Qbar Lean definitions cover only a different coefficient specialization and do not attach the whole finite-E item. All Mathlib queries were actually run; two phrasings found only generic ingredients.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes every clause of def-wf-tate-twist in both master order 2566 and unchanged main-20261015 order 2910: the roots inverse limit and ell-th power transitions; E(1) via its integral lattice; E(0), positive tensor powers, negative derived duals and their induced Weil arrows; the Tate twist endofunctor. The enclosing cyclotomic unit is a definition with no proof steps, and this item is not its key node. Related ordinary/condensed coefficient twists omit these finite-stage Weil pairs and are not identical definitions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q111-e4644082c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes. Shape (A): the delivery is one commit containing the item and its report; review_split gives PASS with 0 new nodes. Base: the item was 'imported' in an earlier run's snapshot and in both clones (live, side-live), so this is its first split. It is not superseded, has no repair note, is not dropped, and no SGA source is cited. Source: master order 2566 and main-20261015 order 2910 are verbatim identical apart from frontmatter. The delivered statement keeps every clause of the source (Z_ell(1) as lim mu with ell-power transitions; E(1) = Z_ell(1) tensor E; E(0); derived tensor powers E(m); E(-m) = RHom(E(m), E_X); and (-)(m) = - tensor^L E(m) on WeilD(X_0,E)) and only makes the inherited setting and the Weil maps explicit. I checked all 15 stmt_deps against how the item uses them: the setting matches def-wf-weil-category; mu, the transitions and the module structure come from def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf; the limit from def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit; local freeness of the lattice and Zl-hat tensor R = B from lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free clauses 2 and 3. Membership in the integral category comes from lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization, (ii) implies (i), with one stratum and P = R[0]; its hypotheses hold because X is of finite type over k, hence noetherian and finite-dimensional, with ell != p invertible. The maps c_r come from def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image and lem-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image-iso clauses 1-3. tau_B comes from lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image clauses 2 and 3 and is the same map as the coefficient identification in def-wf-automorphism-completed-transport and def-wf-tensor-product. The extension to L_R uses sigma from lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom; its semilinearity over tau_B is a short check from clause 2 plus naturality. The tensor and internal-Hom Weil maps come from def-wf-tensor-product and def-wf-internal-hom (the latter uses phi_K^{-1} contravariantly), and restriction to WeilD from lem-wf-tensor-weil and lem-wf-internal-hom-weil. The full dependency closure (11,899 nodes) does not contain the item, so there is no cycle. Duplicate search: def-coefficient-twists-detailed has no Weil structure and is cited for the lattice; def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists is a separate blueprint node in D^b_{c,W}(Y,Lambda) with sheaf-level powers, related but not the same definition (advisory only: a future comparison of the two Weil structures may be worth recording); sk-def-sp-tate-twist uses another coefficient model. The slopmaster2 TateTwist.lean declarations build Qbar constant Weil twists, not this finite-E definition, so they are not an exact attachment; keeping the record unchanged is right. Edge cases checked: m = 0, 1, -1; E = Q_ell; ramified E (the ell-power tower against the varpi-power tower, reconciled by clause 3); X empty; the geometric-Frobenius convention. Three kinds of Mathlib search are recorded (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep), all with no match.
